import math

# Data for the four months (in millions of current foreign-currency units)
belgian_francs = [12060, 2245, 16408, 13327]
canadian_dollars = [10371, 10724, 11176, 10806]

# Calculate Pearson correlation coefficient
n = len(belgian_francs)

# Means
mean_bf = sum(belgian_francs) / n
mean_cd = sum(canadian_dollars) / n

# Calculate numerator (covariance) and denominators (standard deviations)
numerator = sum((belgian_francs[i] - mean_bf) * (canadian_dollars[i] - mean_cd) for i in range(n))
denom_bf = math.sqrt(sum((x - mean_bf)**2 for x in belgian_francs))
denom_cd = math.sqrt(sum((x - mean_cd)**2 for x in canadian_dollars))

# Pearson correlation
r = numerator / (denom_bf * denom_cd)

print(f'Belgian Francs: {belgian_francs}')
print(f'Canadian Dollars: {canadian_dollars}')
print(f'Mean Belgian Francs: {mean_bf}')
print(f'Mean Canadian Dollars: {mean_cd}')
print(f'Pearson correlation coefficient: {r}')
print(f'Rounded to 4 decimal places: {round(r, 4)}')
"
